body.statement: Construct one total test that, using the lexicographically first minimizer in \(\mathcal K_n\), has rejection probability at most \(a_0\) uniformly on \(\mathcal H_0\) for every \(n\), type-II error at most \(b_0\) whenever \(D(P)\ge C r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\), deterministic tuning, and stated arithmetic and memory costs through dense and sparse occupancy regimes. A valid target cost is \(O(|\mathcal K_n|n+\sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) arithmetic and \(O(\max_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) memory, with any sharper certified implementation recorded. Next prove \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\) with constants depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\). Only after that equivalence is established, denote their common order by \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}(n;\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), simplify it in every regime including equality-case logarithms, and conclude \(\rho_n^*\asymp r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\). If the two deterministic optimizations do not match, state the remaining upper--lower gap instead of defining a common rate.
body.justification: This remains the field-tier theorem target: it requires a total uniformly calibrated test and an original fixed-\(n\), constant-null-supported converse on the identical class, followed by an independent optimization match.
body.gap: The exact nested binary likelihood now identifies both the one-observation matching equation and a surviving two-observation coefficient for the simplest bounded coefficient laws. What is missing is a realizable solution of the complete moment system, a proved all-order divergence bound, and the matching sparse-occupancy corrected-energy concentration theorem; the frozen handles cannot substitute for these steps.
body.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying any fitted forest or converting non-rejection into a homogeneity conclusion.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct bounded null and alternative coefficient laws satisfying the complete likelihood-moment system generated by the nested macro--fine expansion, prove a fixed-\(n\) same-class divergence bound for every positive-separation feasible tuple, construct and calibrate the matching nested corrected-energy test through all sparse occupancies, and optimize the two independently defined finite maps in every regime.
obligation.obstruction: The exact product likelihood contains treatment-effect correction factors multiplied by the random propensity perturbation. Outer-sign averaging cancels the terms linear in the macro sign, but a direct bounded-Rademacher implementation leaves the explicit two-observation coefficient in equation (12) of the partial result. No bounded atomic pair of laws has yet been constructed that satisfies every further moment equation while preserving the original Hölder and margin constraints, and no total statistic with matching order-two through order-four collision concentration has been proved. Therefore neither a same-class converse nor a matching achievability map is presently available, and defining \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) would be circular.
obligation.attempted: The calculation expands all four binary cell probabilities relative to an interior reference, writes the exact prior-predictive \(n\)-fold products for the nested construction, verifies conditional one-observation matching, computes the first nonmatching two-observation coefficient for bounded Rademacher marginals, stress-tests its scale at \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), and solves the signal-dependent first-projection inequality for any prospective corrected-energy statistic. The simple Rademacher realization is rejected unless additional moment matching cancels its displayed quadratic term.
obligation.partial_result:
The strongest conclusion presently justified on the unchanged class is the proved bracket.  With
\[
t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\},\qquad
b_n=\begin{cases}
n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\leq4t,\\
n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t,
\end{cases}
\]
the already established results give constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\), such that
\[
c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq \rho_n^*\leq Cb_n,
\qquad n\geq n_0.                                                     \tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\quad\hbox{and}\quad d\leq4\gamma
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},             \tag{2}
\]
and the boundary \(d=4\gamma\) in this proved subregion carries no logarithm.

Here is the exact likelihood calculation obtained for the proposed nested repair.  Work first at one covariate value relative to the interior reference
\[
e_*={1\over2},\qquad m_{0,*}={3\over8},\qquad \tau_*={1\over8}.
\]
The four reference conditional cell probabilities, in the order \((a,y)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), are
\[
p^*_{00}={5\over16},\qquad p^*_{01}={3\over16},
\qquad p^*_{10}=p^*_{11}={1\over4}.                                  \tag{3}
\]
Define
\[
s_e(a)=2(2a-1),qquad
s_b(a,y)=
\begin{cases}
-8/5,&(a,y)=(0,0),\\
 8/3,&(a,y)=(0,1),\\
-2,&(a,y)=(1,0),\\
 2,&(a,y)=(1,1).
\end{cases}                                                          \tag{4}
\]
For a constant-effect null component with \(e=1/2+u\), \(m_0=3/8+v\), and \(\tau=1/8\), direct multiplication of the four Bernoulli cells gives the exact, not asymptotic, likelihood ratio
\[
L_0(a,y\mid x)=\{1+s_e(a)u(x)\}\{1+s_b(a,y)v(x)\}.                  \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, for example,
\[
{(1/2-u)(3/8+v)\over3/16}
=1-2u+{8\over3}v-{16\over3}uv,
\]
and the other three cells give the remaining rows of (4).

Let \(Q\) be a macro cell with outer sign \(\sigma_Q\), let \((B_j)_{j\subset Q}\) be fine-scale bumps satisfying
\[
G_Q=\sum_{j\subset Q}B_j^2,
\]
and put
\[
u_k=\sum_jU_{k,j}B_j,qquad v_k=\sum_jV_{k,j}B_j,qquad k\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Conditional on the outer signs, suppose the coefficient pairs are independent across \(j\), have zero coordinate means, and obey
\[
\mathbb E_0(U_{0,j}V_{0,j})-
\mathbb E_1(U_{1,j}V_{1,j})=\delta\sigma_Q.                           \tag{6}
\]
Give the alternative component
\[
e_1={1\over2}+u_1,qquad
m_{0,1}={3\over8}+v_1-2\delta\sigma_QG_Q,qquad
\tau_1={1\over8}+4\delta\sigma_QG_Q.                                \tag{7}
\]
Every null component still has exactly constant effect \(1/8\).  Equation (7) makes the alternative arm-regression perturbation equal to \(v_1+2(2a-1)\delta\sigma_QG_Q\); hence its exact likelihood ratio is
\[
L_1(a,y\mid x)=
\{1+s_e(a)u_1(x)\}
\{1+s_b(a,y)v_1(x)+s_e(a)s_b(a,y)\delta\sigma_QG_Q(x)\}.             \tag{8}
\]
Equations (5)--(8), zero means, and the square-partition identity imply, for every \((a,y,x)\),
\[
\mathbb E_0\{L_0(a,y\mid x)\mid\sigma\}
=\mathbb E_1\{L_1(a,y\mid x)\mid\sigma\}.                          \tag{9}
\]
Thus the architecture really does match one observation conditional on the outer signs; this conclusion is not being inferred from a construction label.

The full fixed-sample comparison required by the converse is nevertheless
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline L_{0,n}
&=\mathbb E_{\sigma}\mathbb E_0
  \prod_{i=1}^n\{1+s_{e,i}u_0(X_i)\}
                    \{1+s_{b,i}v_0(X_i)\},\\
\overline L_{1,n}
&=\mathbb E_{\sigma}\mathbb E_1
  \prod_{i=1}^n\{1+s_{e,i}u_1(X_i)\}
  \{1+s_{b,i}v_1(X_i)+s_{e,i}s_{b,i}\delta\sigma_{Q(X_i)}G_{Q(X_i)}(X_i)\}.
                                                                            \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
Formula (10) displays every occurrence of the treatment-effect amplitude: choosing a correction term at an index contributes one factor \(\delta\sigma_QG_Q\), and choosing the propensity factor at the same index additionally contributes \(s_{e,i}u_1(X_i)\delta\sigma_QG_Q\).  Consequently those terms cannot lawfully be placed in an unspecified degree-at-least-five remainder.

There is already a sharp early-kill calculation for the most elementary bounded coefficient choice.  Consider one active fine coordinate, write \(B_i=B(X_i)\), and set
\[
x_i=s_{e,i}B_i,qquad y_i=s_{b,i}B_i,qquad k_i=x_iy_i,qquad
r=\delta\sigma_Q.
\]
Let both experiments have Rademacher marginals with
\(\mathbb E U^2=q_e^2\) and \(\mathbb E V^2=q_b^2\); take the null correlation \(\mathbb E_0(UV)=r\) and the alternative correlation \(\mathbb E_1(UV)=0\).  The alternative also uses the correction in (7).  Symmetry makes the mixed moments with exactly one odd exponent vanish, and fixed magnitudes give \(\mathbb E U^2V^2=q_e^2q_b^2\) on both sides.  Exact expansion for two observations supported on this coordinate yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_0(L_{0,1}L_{0,2})
={}&1+x_1x_2q_e^2+y_1y_2q_b^2
+(x_1+x_2)(y_1+y_2)r
+x_1x_2y_1y_2q_e^2q_b^2,\\
\mathbb E_1(L_{1,1}L_{1,2})
={}&(1+x_1x_2q_e^2)
\{(1+k_1r)(1+k_2r)+y_1y_2q_b^2\}.
                                                                            \tag{11}
\end{aligned}
\]
Averaging (11) over the symmetric outer sign cancels every term linear in \(r\), but it leaves
\[
\mathbb E_{\sigma}\!\left[
\mathbb E_0(L_{0,1}L_{0,2})-
\mathbb E_1(L_{1,1}L_{1,2})
\right]
=-\delta^2 k_1k_2(1+q_e^2x_1x_2).                                    \tag{12}
\]
Thus outer-sign averaging alone is insufficient: the coefficient laws must satisfy additional, explicitly derived two-observation moment equations that cancel (12), or the divergence envelope must charge it.  This is the first nonmatching term for this bounded Rademacher implementation.

At the mandated stress point \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), the smoothness constraints for the nested architecture are
\[
\delta\lesssim h^{1/5},\qquad \delta\lesssim H.
\]
At equality they give \(h\asymp\delta^5\) and \(H\asymp\delta\).  The paired fine-collision scale associated with (12) is then
\[
n^2h\delta^4\asymp n^2\delta^9,                                     \tag{13}
\]
whereas the proposed four-observation collision scale is
\[
n^4h^2H\delta^4\asymp n^4\delta^{15}.                               \tag{14}
\]
The latter balances at \(\delta\asymp n^{-4/15}\), and at that value (13) is \(n^{-2/5}\), hence negligible.  In contrast, an uncancelled macro term would equal
\[
n^2H\delta^4\asymp n^2\delta^5=n^{2/3}                              \tag{15}
\]
at \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\).  Therefore a lower construction claiming the rough rate from (14) must prove exact cancellation of (15); bounding it cannot suffice.  Equations (12)--(15) are a diagnostic, not a converse theorem, because existence of bounded coefficient laws satisfying all remaining moment equations and a support-controlled all-order expansion has not been proved.

The upper-handle rate calculus can also be corrected without presuming the missing statistic.  If a corrected energy statistic has population signal \(\mu\), approximation bias \(B\), and on a calibration event satisfies
\[
\mu\geq c_0(D(P)-B)_+^2,qquad
|T-\mu|\leq C_0\{\sqrt{\mu\Lambda_n/n}+E_n\},                       \tag{16}
\]
then
\[
C_0\sqrt{\mu\Lambda_n/n}
\leq {\mu\over2}+{C_0^2\Lambda_n\over2n}.                           \tag{17}
\]
Consequently the first-projection contribution after solving the signal-dependent inequality is of distance order at most \((\Lambda_n/n)^{1/2}\), not \((\Lambda_n/n)^{1/4}\); the other contribution is \(E_n^{1/2}\).  What remains unproved is precisely a total statistic on the original sample for which (16) holds with all order-two through order-four nested occupancy terms and a uniform level allocation.

No common \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) is defined by these calculations.  The unresolved work is to solve the finite coefficient moment system exposed by (10)--(12), prove its bounded-support remainder and same-class membership, derive the matching corrected-energy concentration inequality including sparse occupancy, and optimize the resulting independent lower and upper maps.  Until those steps are supplied, (1)--(2) are the complete proved rate claims.
